newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-KARLSSON WINS WOMEN'S 200 MEDLEY WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-KARLSSON WINS WOMEN'S 200 MEDLEY WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Louise Karlsson gave Swedish fans plenty to cheer about when she won the women's 200 metres individual medley gold to provide the host nation with their third title of the world short-course championships on Sunday.

Karlsson, bronze medallist at the last edition of the championships in Rio de Janeiro in 1995, seized control from the start and led comfortably through the butterfly, backstroke and breaststroke legs.
But she faced a withering challenge from Slovakian freestyle specialist Martina Moravcova on the final freestyle leg.
Moravcova closed the gap down the last length of the 25-metre pool but Karlsson just clung on to win in two minutes 11.19 seconds.
Moravcova was just 0.02 seconds adrift and left with the silver medal to add to the bronze she took in Friday's 200 freestyle.

Britain's Sue Rolph, gold medallist at the European short-course championships in Rostock last December, gained the bronze in 2:12.39, touching just ahead of Germany's 400 individual medley silver medallist Sabine Herbst (2:12.72).
